examples.name: ApiServer
examples.title: Address an existing server by socket
examples.description: Construct a Server for the fixture's socket and list its sessions. Server is a value that addresses a tmux daemon; constructing it does not start or stop that daemon.

examples.name: ApiSessions
examples.title: List session snapshots
examples.description: Create two sessions and read the server-wide listing. Sort by name for this display; the API itself returns tmux's order. The fixture also owns a bootstrap session.

examples.name: ApiWindows
examples.title: List windows across the server
examples.description: Create editor and logs windows, then find them in the server-wide listing. Each window appears once even if linked into several sessions; use windowLinks() when session-local indexes matter.

examples.name: ApiPanes
examples.title: Find a window's panes
examples.description: Read all panes and select those whose windowID matches a newly created window. Pane values are snapshots; reading a property does not query tmux again.

examples.name: ApiNewSession
examples.title: Create a session and refresh its snapshot
examples.description: Create a detached session with an editor window, add a logs window, then look up the session by its stable ID. The original Session still reports one window; the fresh snapshot reports two.

examples.name: ApiNewWindow
examples.title: Create a window at an explicit index
examples.description: Create a logs window at index 3. newWindow returns a WindowAppearance containing the global window and its session-local WindowLink. An occupied index fails instead of silently replacing another window.

examples.name: ApiSplitPane
examples.title: Split a specific pane
examples.description: Split the fixture's pane to the right and give the new pane 40 percent of its width. Address the pane itself so a different active pane cannot change the target.

examples.name: ApiQueryPanes
examples.title: Filter panes with a typed expression
examples.description: Create an inactive split and ask for active panes using a FilterExpr built from a Swift key path. The server evaluates the filter and returns matching Pane snapshots; the original pane stays active.

examples.name: ApiCapture
examples.title: Send input and capture its output
examples.description: Type a printf command literally, send Enter as a key, and wait for its output. Compare a complete output row so terminal echo cannot satisfy the check. The five-second deadline bounds the example; the 25-millisecond pause avoids busy polling.
